allies.rationale_text: Critical-mass helps compounding distinguish between early accumulation and the threshold where gains start accelerating.
allies.affinity_rationale: Threshold concept — 'the threshold needed before rapid growth and compounding can occur. Once critical mass is reached, the positive effects begin to accelerate and compound' — critical mass defines when compounding shifts from linear to exponential.
allies.activation_condition: When early-stage effort has not yet reached the threshold where compound acceleration begins and understanding the distance to critical mass is needed to maintain patience and investment

allies.rationale_text: Feedback-loops explain how repeated gains or losses become self-reinforcing over time.
allies.source_quote: continuous improvement is achieved through feedback loops
allies.affinity_rationale: Self-reinforcing mechanism — 'continuous improvement is achieved through feedback loops' — feedback loops ARE the mechanism through which compounding gains become self-reinforcing over time.
allies.activation_condition: When compounding depends on outputs being fed back as inputs that amplify subsequent cycles, and understanding the feedback structure is needed to protect or accelerate the compounding engine

allies.rationale_text: Margin-of-safety gives compounding the downside protection needed to preserve the base that future gains depend on.
allies.source_quote: protecting downside is as important as amplifying upside
allies.affinity_rationale: Protective complement — 'protecting downside is as important as amplifying upside' — preserves the base that future compounding depends on, but operates as a defensive mechanism rather than the compounding engine itself.
allies.activation_condition: When the base on which compounding depends is at risk and downside protection is needed to prevent a loss that would reset the accumulated compound gains

antagonists.rationale_text: Confirmation-bias turns compounding dangerous when people keep scaling a flawed thesis instead of checking whether the foundation is wrong.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Scaling risk — causes 'teams to keep scaling a flawed thesis instead of checking whether the foundation is wrong' — compounding a flawed thesis makes confirmation bias especially dangerous because the error also compounds.
antagonists.activation_condition: When compound growth is being projected forward without checking whether the foundational thesis is actually correct, because confirming evidence is being sought while disconfirming signals are ignored

structured_tensions.tension_text: Compounding conflicts with optionality when commitment to a compounding path forecloses pivots that would redirect effort toward a higher-yielding trajectory.
structured_tensions.source_quote: compounding conflicts with optionality (optionality) when commitment to a compounding path forecloses pivots that would redirect effort toward a higher-yielding trajectory.

structured_tensions.tension_text: Compounding conflicts with margin-of-safety when projecting compound growth rates forward without accounting for the fragility of the base that sustains them.
structured_tensions.source_quote: compounding conflicts with margin-of-safety (margin of safety) when projecting compound growth rates forward without accounting for the fragility of the base that sustains them.
